subject: Food Science
title: Major Food Recalls
description: A 60-second lesson on Major Food Recalls.

hook.text: In 2008, the Peanut Corporation of America knowingly shipped Salmonella-positive peanuts. The CEO went to prison for 28 years.

buildup.text: Food recalls are classified by severity: Class I (serious health risk), Class II (remote risk), Class III (label violation only).

discovery.text: A Class I recall can remove millions of products from stores within 48 hours. Supply chains reverse direction overnight.

twist.text: Voluntary recalls account for 99% of all recalls. Companies act before the FDA orders—reputation damage costs more.

climax.text: The largest US food recall ever: 143 million pounds of beef in 2008 after video showed sick cattle entering the food supply.

punchline.text: Recalls save lives but destroy brands. Prevention beats pulling millions of units.

quiz.question: Why do companies almost always recall food voluntarily?
options: Reputational damage from an FDA-ordered recall is far worse than voluntary action
